title: Santa's Speedy Shopper: raise Kimi K3.1 Pro's mean tokens/sec on a real gift-finding task
additional_information: The candidate is an OpenClaw agent's instructions (shopper/AGENTS.md) and request settings (shopper/settings.json); read README.md first. The judge sends them to a bench service that runs the agent on Kimi K3.1 Pro on Cerebras with OpenClaw and scores it like the official Speed Bounty patch: the mean over model calls of completion_tokens / completion_time (Cerebras server-side decode timing). A run is valid only if the agent's answer lists five real, live product pages that came from its own search results in that run; URLs written into shopper/ are forbidden. Per-call speed is noisy (about 270-560 tok/s on identical requests, from shared serving load), hence 3 runs per cell and a 5% minimum effect. Ideas worth testing: how much the agent writes per call (short tool-call turns vs long answers), number of model calls (one search call vs several), reasoning effort (low/high/max) and how much it reasons, sampling settings, and output style (predictable, structured text may decode faster with speculative decoding). Every judged run costs real API tokens under a 100K tokens/minute limit, and the judge takes minutes per run.
